title: Identity Cards of the Marrow: Stem-Cell Markers, Light-Chain Order and Helper T Subsets
summary: Read the three identity cards of blood-cell production: the CD34+CD38−CD45RA−CD90+CD49f+ gate that enriches (but does not define) long-term human haematopoietic stem cells, the chromosome 14 then 2 then 22 order of immunoglobulin gene rearrangement with class switching that keeps the V-D-J, and the helper T subsets named by their cytokines.

reviewer.note: Teaches Ch. 32 Hit 4 (human HSC immunophenotype), Hit 14 (light-chain rearrangement order after heavy-chain V-D-J; isotype switching by DNA deletion) and Hit 15 (Th1/Th2/Th17/iTreg cytokines). Marker phenotype checked against Belluschi 2018 and Bari 2018; rarity and gradient staining against Zonari 2017; rearrangement order, chromosomes and class switch recombination against Lefranc 2020 and Collins 2018; helper T cytokines and their plasticity against Geginat 2014. Two qualifications are taught and flagged: the marker gate enriches rather than defines long-term HSC (register flag rv-ch32-hsc-gate-enrichment) and helper subsets are plastic rather than fixed lineages (register flag rv-ch32-th-subset-plasticity). Not taught: the Ch. 32 Number Vault table, Trap 4 (megaloblastic change), somatic hypermutation detail, thymic selection.
reviewer.locationsNote: High-Yield Hits numbered in reviewer order: Hit 4 is the HSC immunophenotype bullet, Hit 14 the B-cell light-chain bullet, Hit 15 the Th-subset bullet.

objectives: State the surface-marker combination that enriches long-term repopulating human haematopoietic stem cells, and why it enriches rather than defines them.
Put immunoglobulin gene rearrangement in order: heavy chain on chromosome 14, then kappa on chromosome 2, then lambda on chromosome 22, and explain what class switch recombination deletes.
Match each helper T subset to its signature cytokines and target pathogens, and state why the subsets are plastic.

scenes.title: Three identity checks
scenes.altText: Invented scenario. Three bench puzzles on one screen: (1) a research sort has already gated lineage-negative CD34+CD38- cord blood cells and asks which further markers enrich the long-term stem cell; (2) a B-cell precursor has a productive heavy-chain rearrangement and a pre-B-cell receptor on its surface, and the question is which locus rearranges next and on which chromosome; (3) a helper T-cell clone secretes interferon-gamma, and the question is which class of pathogen it is built to fight. Question token: "Which markers, which locus, which cytokine?"

cues.text: Three identity checks. First, a sort has already gated lineage-negative, CD34 positive, CD38 negative cord blood cells, and asks which extra markers enrich the long-term stem cell.
Second, a B-cell precursor already carries a productive heavy chain and a pre-B-cell receptor. Which locus rearranges next, and on which chromosome?
Third, a helper T-cell clone secretes interferon gamma. Which class of pathogen is it built to fight? Markers, locus, cytokine.

props.label: Which markers, which locus, which cytokine?

scenes.title: Three identity cards
scenes.altText: Identity cards. Stem-cell gate (Belluschi 2018; Bari 2018): the long-term repopulating human haematopoietic stem cell is enriched in the CD34+CD38-CD45RA-CD90+CD49f+ fraction, with lineage markers negative; CD49f and CD90 expression separate long-term (49f+) from short-term (49f-) repopulating cells. Rarity card (Zonari 2017): no more than about 0.1% of lineage-negative cord blood cells engraft long term, and roughly 0.01% of infused CD34+ cells contribute to long-term haematopoiesis in gene-therapy patients. B-cell card (Lefranc 2020): the IGH locus on chromosome 14 rearranges D-J then V-D-J; a productive rearrangement gives a cytoplasmic mu heavy chain, which pairs with IGLL1 and VPREB1 as the pre-B-cell receptor, and that receptor both stops further heavy-chain rearrangement and starts light-chain rearrangement. Helper T card (Geginat 2014, Table 1): Th1 CXCR3+, interferon gamma, T-bet, intracellular pathogens; Th2 GATA-3, interleukin 4, 5 and 13, extracellular parasites; Th17 CCR6+CD161+, interleukin 17, 22 and 26, RORC2, extracellular bacteria and fungi; regulatory T cells CD25+CD127-, TGF-beta, FOXP3, self-tolerance.

cues.text: Card one, the stem-cell gate. Among lineage-negative cells, the long-term repopulating human stem cell is enriched in the CD34 positive, CD38 negative, CD45RA negative, CD90 positive, CD49f positive fraction.

That cell is rare. No more than about one in a thousand lineage-negative cord blood cells engrafts long term, and in gene-therapy patients only about one in ten thousand infused CD34 positive cells contributes to long-term blood production.

Card two, the B cell. The heavy-chain locus on chromosome 14 joins D to J, then V to D-J. A productive rearrangement makes a mu chain that pairs with two surrogate light chains as the pre-B-cell receptor, which stops further heavy-chain rearrangement and starts light-chain rearrangement.

Card three, the helper T cells. Th1 makes interferon gamma for intracellular pathogens, Th2 makes interleukins 4, 5 and 13 for parasites, Th17 makes interleukin 17 for extracellular bacteria and fungi, and regulatory T cells use transforming growth factor beta to keep self-tolerance.

props.label: ≤ 0.1% of Lin− cord blood cells engraft long term

scenes.title: The order, the editing, the switch
scenes.altText: Sequence cards (Lefranc 2020; Collins 2018). Order: light-chain V-J rearrangement of the IGK locus usually precedes IGL. One chromosome 2 rearranges first; if productive, a kappa chain is made, and the other chromosome 2 and both chromosomes 22 stay germline. If unproductive, the other chromosome 2 is tried, then chromosome 22. Editing: repeated kappa rearrangements can continue on one chromosome until the possibilities are exhausted; kappa deleting elements downstream of IGKC can terminate kappa rearrangement and drive the cell to the lambda locus, and the human lambda locus has no such deletional element, so serial lambda rearrangement is possible. Isotypic exclusion: one light-chain type per cell, and the excluded allele is usually germline or unproductively rearranged, typically the IGK locus in a lambda-expressing cell. Switch: switch sequences about 2 kb upstream of each IGHC gene except IGHD; recombination between S-mu and a downstream S region deletes the intervening DNA, so the same rearranged V-D-J is now transcribed with a downstream constant gene, giving IgG, IgA or IgE with unchanged specificity. IgD is produced by a splicing mechanism, not by class switching.

cues.text: Now the order. Light-chain rearrangement starts in the kappa locus on chromosome 2. If that first rearrangement is productive, a kappa chain is made and the other chromosome 2 and both copies of chromosome 22 stay germline.
If it is unproductive, the cell tries the other chromosome 2, then chromosome 22, the lambda locus. Kappa deleting elements can end kappa rearrangement early and push the cell to lambda.
One light-chain type per cell: the excluded locus is usually germline or unproductively rearranged, classically the kappa locus in a lambda-expressing cell.

Then the switch. Switch sequences sit about two kilobases upstream of each heavy-chain constant gene except delta. Recombination between the mu switch region and a downstream one deletes the DNA in between, so the same rearranged V-D-J is read with a new constant gene, and specificity does not change.

props.label: Kappa deleting element → drives cell to λ (chr 22)

props.title: Class switch recombination
lines: S regions ≈ 2 kb 5′ of each IGHC
S-mu joins downstream S: DNA deleted

scenes.title: What the markers really tell you
scenes.altText: Interpretation cards. Gate card (Zonari 2017): CD38, CD49f and CD90 stain as a gradient of increasing antigen density rather than two clean populations, so cells of intermediate phenotype fall outside binary sorting gates and gate placement changes who is counted as a stem cell. Heterogeneity card (Belluschi 2018): within the CD19-CD34+CD38-CD45RA-CD49f+CD90+ stem-cell compartment, the first lineage-restriction events already generate myelo-lymphoid committed cells with no erythroid output, so a pure gate is not a functionally uniform cell. Light-chain card (Lefranc 2020): a lambda-expressing B cell usually has its kappa locus germline or unproductively rearranged, and only one chromosome 14 plus one chromosome 2 or 22 is productively rearranged. Plasticity card (Geginat 2014): Th1 cells can acquire interleukin 10 production, Th17 cells are relatively unstable, and FOXP3 regulatory T cells can acquire T-bet and interferon gamma, so a single cytokine measured once does not fix a lineage.

cues.text: What do the markers really tell you? CD38, CD49f and CD90 stain as a gradient, not as two clean populations, so where you draw the gate changes which cells you call stem cells.
And the gate is not functionally uniform. Inside that stem-cell compartment, the first lineage restriction has already happened in some cells, producing myelo-lymphoid cells with no red-cell output.
On the B-cell side, a lambda-expressing cell usually has its kappa locus germline or unproductively rearranged, and only one heavy-chain and one light-chain allele is productive.

On the T-cell side, subsets are not sealed boxes. Th1 cells can start making interleukin 10, Th17 cells are relatively unstable, and FOXP3 regulatory T cells can acquire T-bet and interferon gamma, so one cytokine measured once does not fix a lineage.

props.title: Helper subsets are plastic
lines: FOXP3 Treg can gain T-bet and IFN-γ

scenes.title: Three classic traps
scenes.altText: Three trap cards: "CD34+CD38− means pure stem cells" (✓ the markers stain as gradients and only a minute fraction of CD34+ cells engraft long term, so the gate enriches rather than defines); "Lambda rearranges first" (✓ heavy-chain V-D-J on chromosome 14 comes first, then kappa on chromosome 2, then lambda on chromosome 22); "Isotype switching changes the antibody specificity" (✓ switch recombination deletes the DNA between switch regions and keeps the same V-D-J, so only the constant region changes).

cues.text: Trap one: CD34 positive, CD38 negative means pure stem cells. No. The markers stain as gradients, and only a minute fraction of CD34 positive cells engraft long term. The gate enriches rather than defines.
Trap two: lambda rearranges first. No. The heavy chain on chromosome 14 goes first, then kappa on chromosome 2, then lambda on chromosome 22.
Trap three: isotype switching changes the specificity. No. Switching deletes the DNA between switch regions and keeps the same V-D-J, so only the constant region changes.

scenes.title: Fourteen, two, twenty-two
scenes.altText: Memory aid: "FOURTEEN, TWO, TWENTY-TWO. Heavy chain on chromosome 14 first, kappa on 2, lambda on 22 — and the switch cuts out constant-region DNA, never the V-D-J. At the stem-cell gate, 34, 90 and 49f point UP while 38 and 45RA point DOWN. For helper T cells, 1 goes INSIDE, 2 hits the WORMS, 17 holds the OUTSIDE wall, and Treg keeps the PEACE." Tokens: 14 → 2 → 22 · 34/90/49f up, 38/45RA down · Th1 inside, Th2 worms, Th17 outside. A card lists where the aid breaks.

cues.text: Memory aid: fourteen, two, twenty-two. Heavy chain on chromosome 14 first, kappa on 2, lambda on 22, and the switch cuts out constant-region DNA, never the V-D-J. At the stem-cell gate, 34, 90 and 49f point up, while 38 and 45RA point down. For helper T cells, one goes inside, two hits the worms, seventeen holds the outside wall, and the regulatory cell keeps the peace.

Where it breaks: the gate enriches long-term stem cells rather than defining them, and those markers stain as gradients; kappa before lambda is the usual order, not a law; and helper subsets are plastic, sharing cytokines and switching profiles.

props.label: Lin− CD34+ CD38− CD45RA− CD90+ CD49f+ enriches long-term HSC
Heavy 14 → κ 2 → λ 22 · switch keeps V-D-J · Th1/Th2/Th17/Treg by cytokine

explanation.what: Plain language: blood cells all come from a tiny number of stem cells in the marrow. You cannot see a stem cell down the microscope, so laboratories identify it by the proteins on its surface. Growing B cells cut and paste their antibody genes in a fixed order, first the heavy chain gene, then one of two light chain genes. Helper T cells are sorted into teams by the chemical messengers they release. Scientific terms: haematopoietic stem cell (HSC), lineage-negative, CD34, CD38, CD45RA, CD90 (Thy-1), CD49f (integrin alpha-6), long-term repopulating cell, IGH/IGK/IGL loci, V(D)J rearrangement, pre-B-cell receptor, kappa deleting element, receptor editing, isotypic exclusion, class switch recombination, switch (S) regions, Th1, Th2, Th17, regulatory T cell, FOXP3.
explanation.why: Surface markers are only correlates of function: antibody staining for CD38, CD49f and CD90 produces a gradient of intensity rather than two separate populations, so the long-term stem cell is enriched by a gate rather than captured by it, and lineage restriction can already be under way inside that gate. In B cells the pre-B-cell receptor is the switchboard: once a productive heavy chain reaches the surface it stops further heavy-chain rearrangement and starts light-chain rearrangement, which is why heavy chain always precedes light chain. Class switching works by deleting the DNA between two switch regions, which is why the antigen-binding V-D-J survives while the constant region changes.
explanation.measure: HSC enrichment: lineage markers negative, CD34+, CD38−, CD45RA−, CD90+, CD49f+ (CD49f+ marks long-term, CD49f− short-term repopulating cells). Rarity: no more than ~0.1% of lineage-negative cord blood cells engraft long term; ~0.01% of infused CD34+ cells contribute to long-term haematopoiesis after gene therapy. Rearrangement: IGH at 14q32.33, IGK at 2p11.2, IGL at 22q11.2; D-J then V-D-J at IGH, then V-J at IGK (usually) before IGL. Switch regions sit about 2 kb upstream of each IGHC gene except IGHD. Helper T cells: Th1 interferon gamma with T-bet; Th2 interleukins 4, 5, 10 and 13 with GATA-3; Th17 interleukins 17, 22 and 26 with RORC2; regulatory T cells CD25+CD127− with TGF-beta and FOXP3.
explanation.differs: Enrichment gate versus functional stem cell; CD49f+ (long-term) versus CD49f− (short-term) repopulating cells; kappa locus (chromosome 2, rearranges first, kappa deleting element can end it) versus lambda locus (chromosome 22, rearranged later, no deletional element so serial editing is possible); class switch recombination (deletes constant-region DNA, specificity kept) versus somatic rearrangement (builds the V-D-J in the first place); IgD expression by splicing versus IgG, IgA and IgE by switching.
explanation.examAngle: Expect: pick the stem-cell immunophenotype from marker lists; state the order and chromosomes of immunoglobulin gene rearrangement; recognise that a lambda-expressing B cell has a silenced kappa locus; say what class switching does and does not change; match a cytokine (interferon gamma, interleukin 4 or 5, interleukin 17, TGF-beta) to its helper T subset and pathogen class.

mnemonic.text: FOURTEEN, TWO, TWENTY-TWO: heavy chain on chromosome 14 first, kappa on 2, lambda on 22 — and the switch cuts out constant-region DNA, never the V-D-J. At the stem-cell gate, 34, 90 and 49f point UP while 38 and 45RA point DOWN. For helper T cells, 1 goes INSIDE, 2 hits the WORMS, 17 holds the OUTSIDE wall, and the regulatory cell keeps the PEACE.
mnemonic.explanation: Encodes the rearrangement order with its chromosome numbers, the direction of each stem-cell marker, and the helper T subset assignments.
mnemonic.limitation: The marker gate enriches long-term stem cells rather than defining them, and CD38, CD49f and CD90 stain as gradients rather than on/off populations; kappa before lambda is the usual order, not an absolute law; and helper T subsets are plastic, sharing cytokines and switching profiles rather than behaving as sealed lineages.

analogyLimitations: The three bench puzzles in the opening scene are invented.
“Identity card” overstates the case: surface markers are correlates of function, not identity.
Marker and cytokine lists are simplified; the cited papers give the full panels and subset tables.
takeaway: The lineage-negative CD34 positive CD38 negative CD45RA negative CD90 positive CD49f positive gate enriches rather than defines long-term human stem cells, B cells rearrange the heavy chain on chromosome 14 before kappa on chromosome 2 and lambda on chromosome 22, and helper T subsets are named by the cytokines they make rather than by fixed lineages

questions.stem: A laboratory sorts lineage-negative cord blood cells to enrich long-term repopulating human haematopoietic stem cells. Which marker combination should it gate on?

options.rationale: Correct. Long-term repopulating human HSC are enriched in the CD34+CD38−CD45RA−CD90+CD49f+ fraction; CD49f expression separates long-term from short-term repopulating cells.
Incorrect. Every marker is in the wrong direction; this phenotype excludes the stem-cell compartment.
Incorrect. CD38 and CD45RA positivity with loss of CD90 and CD49f marks more committed progenitors, not long-term stem cells.
Incorrect. CD45RA must be negative and CD90 positive; CD45RA gain marks lymphoid-primed and more committed cells.

questions.stem: A B-cell precursor has a productive heavy-chain rearrangement and expresses a pre-B-cell receptor. Which event happens next, and where?

options.text: V-J rearrangement of the kappa locus on chromosome 2, with lambda on chromosome 22 held in reserve
options.rationale: Correct. The pre-B-cell receptor stops further heavy-chain rearrangement and starts light-chain rearrangement, and the IGK locus on chromosome 2 usually rearranges before IGL on chromosome 22.

options.text: V-J rearrangement of the lambda locus on chromosome 22, because lambda is used first
options.rationale: Incorrect. The kappa locus usually rearranges first; lambda is attempted after the kappa attempts fail or are terminated.

options.text: A second round of heavy-chain V-D-J rearrangement on the other chromosome 14
options.rationale: Incorrect. Pre-B-cell receptor expression is the signal that inhibits further heavy-chain V-D-J rearrangement.

options.text: Class switch recombination to IgG before any light chain is made
options.rationale: Incorrect. Class switching happens in mature B cells after antigenic stimulation, not before a light chain exists.

questions.stem: A memory B cell has switched from IgM to IgG1. Which statement about that switch and about helper T support is correct?

options.text: Recombination between switch regions deleted the intervening DNA, so the same V-D-J is now expressed with a downstream constant gene and the specificity is unchanged
options.rationale: Correct. Class switch recombination joins the mu switch region to a downstream switch region, deleting the DNA in between while keeping the rearranged V-D-J, so only the constant region changes.

options.text: Switching rebuilt the V-D-J region, so the antibody now binds a different antigen
options.rationale: Incorrect. The rearranged V-D-J is retained; switching changes the constant region, not the antigen-binding specificity.

options.text: Switching to IgG uses the same splicing mechanism that produces IgD
options.rationale: Incorrect. IgD expression depends on a splicing mechanism, whereas IgG, IgA and IgE arise by class switch recombination.

options.text: Th17 cells, through interleukin 17, are the subset defined as the helpers against intracellular pathogens
options.rationale: Incorrect. Th17 cells and interleukin 17 are associated with extracellular bacteria and fungi; interferon-gamma-producing Th1 cells are the subset associated with intracellular pathogens.

claims.text: Long-term repopulating human HSC are enriched in the lineage-negative CD34+CD38−CD45RA−CD90+CD49f+ fraction, with CD49f separating long-term from short-term repopulating cells.

The gate enriches rather than defines: markers stain as gradients, long-term engrafting cells are a minute fraction of CD34+ cells, and lineage-restricted erythroid-null cells already sit inside the CD49f+ compartment.

IGH on chromosome 14 rearranges D-J then V-D-J; the pre-B-cell receptor stops heavy-chain rearrangement and starts light-chain rearrangement; IGK on chromosome 2 usually precedes IGL on chromosome 22; isotypic exclusion leaves the excluded kappa locus germline or unproductive.

Class switch recombination joins S-mu to a downstream switch region, deleting the intervening DNA and keeping the rearranged V-D-J, so IgG, IgA or IgE carry the same specificity; IgD expression depends on splicing.

Helper T subsets and their cytokines: Th1 interferon gamma for intracellular pathogens, Th2 interleukins 4, 5 and 13 for extracellular parasites, Th17 interleukin 17 for extracellular bacteria and fungi, regulatory T cells TGF-beta and FOXP3 for self-tolerance.
Human helper T subsets are plastic rather than sealed lineages.
The exact lineage-marker cocktail behind “Lin−”, and the single-cell engraftment efficiency of the CD49f+ cell, are not taught here.
claims.note: The sources read define the compartment with CD19− or CD45+ rather than a full lineage cocktail, so no lineage-marker list is taught.

accuracyFlags.issue: Ch. 32 Hit 4 presents Lin−CD34+CD38−CD90+CD45RA−CD49f+ as the human HSC immunophenotype to “burn in”. Zonari 2017 shows CD38, CD49f and CD90 stain as gradients rather than two separable populations and that only a minute fraction of CD34+ cells repopulate long term, and Belluschi 2018 shows myelo-lymphoid restricted, erythroid-null cells already arise inside the CD49f+ compartment. The lesson teaches the combination as an enrichment gate, not a definition (register flag rv-ch32-hsc-gate-enrichment).

Ch. 32 Hit 15 assigns one cytokine to each helper T subset. Geginat 2014 reports that human Th2 cells also make interleukins 10 and 13, Th17 cells interleukins 22 and 26, that Th1 cells can acquire interleukin 10 production, that Th17 cells are relatively unstable and that FOXP3+ regulatory T cells can acquire T-bet and interferon gamma, so the subsets are plastic (register flag rv-ch32-th-subset-plasticity).
